claims.description: THR-SPLIT E3. Replaces privacy-lint-{user-paths,vault-name,worker-repo-names,model-id}, which demanded zero occurrences over the whole tracked tree minus four hand-written pathspec exclusions. That claim was unsatisfiable twice over and unverified once: the rule that removes a string must state the string (scripts/path_transform_rule_v1.json), evidence fixed by a digest cannot be edited without breaking the digest that fixes it, and nothing checked that an exclusion was entitled to be one -- docs/adrs/ was excluded wholesale and is where nearly the whole real exposure lives (measured: runs/THR-SPLIT/20260816T013706Z/ESITO-1-what-is-already-public.md). The reformulation: ZERO on the surface a change ADDS (every tracked file whose bytes differ from the declared baseline), EXACTLY the declared count on the surface that already exists (==, not <=, so a public file that grows an occurrence turns this red), and exactly two machine-checkable exemption reasons -- the file is a rule that names what it replaces (hits confined to its own pattern/replacement slots, or, for this declaration itself, each hit being exactly a declared literal), or the file is evidence whose sha256 is pinned by another tracked file. A file in neither is not an exemption. Two classes -- the operator's home path and this host's name -- are COMPUTED from the running process and never written down, so no declaration can name them and none can launder them; that asymmetry is what stops this declaration from becoming the hand-written exclusion it replaces. The --selftest arm is the non-vacuity guard: eleven scratch repositories, each judged as intended, on every run. The last two are the separation itself -- one tree measured twice, differing only in whether it has a remote: a repository with no remote has no public surface, and the day the internal surface gains one, this claim stops being satisfied by emptiness and names what would travel. tests/bypass_ft_internal_enters_public_surface_fixture.sh drives the same boundary independently, and was observed RED with each exemption reason disabled before it was observed green.

claims.description: No tracked file (outside this manifest's four pathspec exclusions) references the operator's numeric uid in the phrase spelling -- the three-letter id-word immediately followed by the token. The token is computed from the running process (id -u) and never written here: a detector that must state the identifier it hunts publishes that identifier in the tracked file that exists to keep it out -- the same asymmetry as its bare-token sibling and the computed classes in scripts/statement_lint.py. Until 2026-08-19 the pattern was anchored with the word-boundary escape under git grep -E, whose ERE engine does not implement that escape: the predicate matched zero lines by construction and could not fail. Corrected to -P and measured at correction time on the tracked tree: zero lines on the surface -- the underlying fact is true, so this claim stays GREEN and, unlike its sibling, declares no exposure. The phrase's occurrences outside the surface (5 lines in 2 files under docs/adrs/ at correction time) sit in the locus the claim's own pathspecs exclude by design.

No tracked file (outside this manifest's four pathspec exclusions) references the operator's numeric uid as a bare id token. The token is computed from the running process (id -u) and never written here: a detector that must state the identifier it hunts publishes that identifier in the tracked file that exists to keep it out -- the asymmetry that makes the home path a computed class in scripts/statement_lint.py and in FT-28. Until 2026-08-19 the pattern was anchored with the word-boundary escape under git grep -E, whose ERE engine does not implement that escape: the predicate matched zero lines by construction and could not fail. Corrected to -P and measured at correction time on the tracked tree: RED, 212 lines across 41 files -- 211 lines in 40 files under runs/THR-SUBAGENT/, 1 line in 1 file under .verity/evidence/. Declared RED as observed, the same discipline the falsifier register applies to a known red (the bypass_ft_bash_unbound and FT-28 rows): this claim is expected to stay RED until the operator records a decision on the exposure it now measures, and a GREEN here means the exposure left the tracked surface. It is declared and not repaired because the repair is not this claim's to take: three of the carrying files are cited by sha256 from tracked conformance records that resolve today, and the order of redaction and re-pinning is an operator decision. 2026-09-04, operator acceptance. The 212 lines across 41 files split along the pin structure, which is why the repair costs one commit and no re-pinning: 211 lines in 40 files under runs/THR-SUBAGENT/ leave this claim's perimeter through a fifth pathspec exclusion, and the one carrier outside that tree -- .verity/evidence/2026-08-01-adr008-testrun/adr008-tmpdir-probe.txt, 1 line -- is redacted at the tip. Those 40 are exactly the carriers fixed by sha256 from tracked records (49 carrier-record-line pairs: 40 rows in INTEGRITY.md, 9 rows across six files under runs/THR-CONFORMANCE/20260814T002404Z/records/), and the redacted one is exactly the carrier no tracked record pins, so no digest goes stale and no second commit is owed. What this GREEN does not say is that the exposure is gone: all 41 files and all 212 lines are already at origin/main, redaction at the tip changes what a fresh clone shows and does not unpublish, and the 40 excluded files keep their 211 lines on the tracked surface. The exclusion states the perimeter in which this rule is applicable -- the tracked surface minus runs/THR-SUBAGENT/ and the four earlier exclusions -- and it was observed refusing before it was accepted: a bare token seeded into a tracked path inside the perimeter turns this claim RED and names that path, while the same token inside runs/THR-SUBAGENT/ does not. An exclusion never seen to refuse would be the vacuous green ADR-018 D3 names at :470-471, and this one is not.

ADR-020 D3: every emitted in-toto Statement conforms to D2's allowlist. Unlike the privacy-lint claims above, this one presides over the EMITTED ARTIFACT and not over the tree -- side-car Statements are written beside the receipt under an ignored directory, so no git grep can ever reach them, which is the defect ADR-020 D1 measured in privacy-lint-user-paths. The --selftest arm is the control: it requires the boundary to accept a conforming specimen and refuse five leaking ones on every run, so the claim still discriminates on a checkout where no run has emitted anything yet. tests/bypass_att_prose_leak_fixture.sh drives the same detector with more arms.
